items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
6 - 10 years of related experience.

Previous supervisory or managerial experience, including responsibility for assigning work, providing performance feedback, developing staff, and supporting employee performance and professional development.
Minimum 6-10 years of progressively responsible related experience in financial analysis, budgeting, fiscal management, financial systems, resource planning, or a related field.
Experience working in a complex higher education, public-sector, or similarly structured organizational environment is highly desirable.
Previous supervisory/managerial experience.

Supervises activities associated with creating, maintaining and reporting on the operational and capital budgets and budget processes, academic and staff budgeted FTE, the performance of financial planning (including problem definition, forecasting, data collection, development of alternative solutions), the performance of human resources FTE planning (position management, staffing forecasting, data collection), development of policy or action recommendations in the areas of budget, finance and human resource planning, and report preparation. (20% time)
Selects, develops, and evaluates personnel to ensure the efficient operation of the function. (15% time)
Conducts presentations of technical information concerning specific projects or schedules. (15% time)
Administers organizational policies that directly affect subordinate employees. (15% time)

Provides comprehensive financial management and oversight for the CHASS Dean's Immediate Office, CHASS Facilities Management, CHASS Student Affairs, and other assigned College units. Monitors financial activity and ensures appropriate budgeting, reconciliation, forecasting, and reporting practices. Reviews financial information to identify unusual activity, discrepancies, potential deficits, compliance concerns, and other issues requiring corrective action. Works with departmental management and financial staff to resolve complex financial issues and develop practical, sustainable solutions. Advises management on appropriate financial practices and the financial implications of operational decisions. Monitors and evaluates the effective use of chart of account elements, including flex fields and other financial attributes. Works in collaboration with the Academic Resource and Budget & Operations Managers during the annual fiscal closing process to ensure that CHASS ends in the best possible financial standing. (15% time)
Ensures that the appropriate internal controls are addressed, maintained and strengthened to protect University resources. (10% time)

Works independently and in collaboration with the CHASS Manager of Budget and Operations on specialized and strategic projects involving College-wide resources, financial planning, organizational analysis, process improvement, systems implementation, and operational effectiveness. Defines project objectives, gathers and analyzes information, evaluates alternatives, develops recommendations, and assists with implementation and monitoring. Leads assigned projects and coordinates with stakeholders across CHASS and campus to ensure timely completion and successful implementation. Provides analytical support for the development and evaluation of college resource allocation approaches, staffing and FTE planning, operating forecasts, and other initiatives requiring complex financial or organizational analysis. Performs other duties and special projects as assigned in support of the College's financial and operational objectives. (10% time)

Extensive knowledge of finance policies, practices and systems, budgeting and reporting techniques, accounting and bookkeeping.
Thorough knowledge and understanding of internal control practices and their impact on protecting University resources.
Demonstrated ability to effectively communicate both verbally and in writing.
Solid understanding of financial and resource planning concepts as well as how to control organizational budgeting.
Extensive knowledge of, human resource policies, practices, and planning.
Client services oriented, has good listening, communication, critical thinking, and analytical skills.
Proven ability to deal with changing priorities and direct the work of others accordingly. Ability to multi-task.
Demonstrated interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively across the organization at all levels.
Ability to prepare and present materials to internal and external constituents.
Demonstrated ability to screen applications, interview candidates, and either make selection decisions or recommend individuals for hire.
Advanced skills in the use of spreadsheet and database software.
